title: fix(security): widen D12 past its receiver-name blind spot and D22(d) past its flat-path one
body:
Two static rules that report clean without enforcing what they document, and the three landed violations they were not seeing. Found by an audit of I1–I30; same defect class as #1216 and #1217, one layer down.

## D12 (I14) — the receiver name was the enforcement

The rule was `/\b(?:this\.|ctx\.)?db\.(?:run|exec)\s*\(/`. `\b` cannot match between the `w` and the `D` of `rawDb`, so **every aliased receiver was invisible** — and `commands/data-delete.ts` has been running two unwrapped `DELETE`s through `input.index.rawDb.run(...)`, on the production `data.delete` IPC path, with `audit:invariants` exiting 0 the whole time.

There was also no rule at all for the prepared-statement form, though `docs/SECURITY-INVARIANTS.md` has named `stmt.run(` an I14 anti-pattern since the invariant was written and `db/write.ts` exports `dbStmtRun` to wrap it. `index/local-index.ts:436` ran an `UPDATE sync_state` through `.query(...).run(...)` — three lines above a compliant `dbRun` INSERT.

**The widening was designed against data, not intuition.** I surveyed all 71 `.run(`/`.exec(` sites in production source first. They are overwhelmingly `RegExp.exec`, plus `AgentCoordinator.run` and `AsyncLocalStorage.run`; the only db-suffixed receivers are real `Database` handles. So the receiver is now any identifier ending in `db`/`Db`/`DB`, which adds no false positives, and the statement form is matched over the whole file because the SQL routinely pushes `.run(` onto its own line.

Turning it on flagged exactly the three predicted sites and nothing else. All three are fixed here.

`embedding-worker.ts` bound a `Database` to `d`, which the convention-keyed rule still cannot see, so it is renamed to `db` and its PRAGMA routed through `dbRun` — matching `local-index.ts:279`, which already does exactly that. That removes the one known-invisible site rather than leaving it as a live example of the bound.

The quantifiers are bounded (`[\w$]{0,64}`) because an unbounded prefix in front of a required literal backtracks quadratically, and this scans every line of every source file.

## D22(d) (I29) — the same blind spot #1216 just fixed for D17

All three emitter patterns ended in `[A-Za-z][\w-]*\.ts`. `[\w-]` cannot cross a `/`, so they matched `../agents/why.ts` and **missed `../agents/briefs/summary.ts` outright**. Grouping emitters into folders — an ordinary refactor — would have taken every emitter out of rule (d)'s sight at once, letting a new surface serve a brief with no `egress_ledger` row while the gate stayed green.

`agents/` holds only `_lib/` today, so nothing is currently escaping. The point is that the rule's shape could not express the property it documents. **This is the identical defect #1216 fixed for D17/I23 one commit earlier** — two rules written in the same style shared it, which is the argument for the subdirectory case being part of the pattern rather than something each rule is trusted to remember.

The `_lib/` lookahead sits immediately after `/agents/`, so it still excludes `agents/_lib/x/y.ts`; there is a test for that direction too.

## Docs

I14's stated rationale was wrong in both directions, so it is corrected rather than propagated. It claimed an unwrapped write means `SQLITE_FULL` "is swallowed silently" and data "can end up half-written without surfacing a typed error". `handleWriteError` (`db/write.ts:75-81`) re-throws unconditionally — a raw `.run()` throws just the same, nothing is swallowed. The real delta is the error's *shape*: a generic `SQLiteError` instead of the typed `DiskFullError`, and no `setDiskSpaceWarning(true)`.

And `DiskFullError`, `isDiskSpaceWarning` and `onDiskFull` have **zero production consumers outside `write.ts`** (verified by grep across `packages/*/src`). Nothing in the gateway branches on a full disk yet, so I14 currently buys consistency and a future seam, not a live behaviour difference. The section now says that. D22(d)'s entry also gains the subdirectory case and the `require()` form, which the rule has matched for a while but the docs never mentioned.

## Red-prove

Each widening was reverted to its pre-fix form and the new tests confirmed red, naming the right thing:

| Mutation | Failing test |
| --- | --- |
| D12 receiver → old `db`-pinned pattern | `flags a dotted alias receiver`, `flags a bare alias receiver`, `flags a capitalised suffix` |
| D12 statement scan disabled | `flags the prepared-statement form, including across a line break` |
| D22(d) static → flat filename pattern | `flags a static emitter import from a SUBDIRECTORY of agents/` |

Both widened patterns also carry a **time-bounded** test. Each puts a quantifier next to a required literal, and a correctness test cannot tell linear from catastrophic backtracking — an argument that a pattern is safe is not a measurement.

The negative side is pinned too: reads through the same statement shape (`.query(...).get(...)`) and the receivers that dominate `.run(`/`.exec(` in this tree are asserted **not** to flag, because a rule that cries wolf gets reverted, which is its own kind of unenforced.

`bun run preflight:fast` — 29/29. `bun test scripts/structure-audit packages/gateway/src/index packages/gateway/src/embedding packages/gateway/test/unit/commands` — 1,590 pass, 0 fail.

title: test(security): make five invariant enforcement tests capable of failing
body:
Five `security-invariants.test.ts` assertions that pass whether or not the invariant holds, and the forged audit row one of them was hiding. Cluster B of the I1–I30 audit; #1218 was cluster A.

For each, the question asked was: **what single edit to production code would break this invariant and leave this test green?** Where I could name one, it is a finding.

## I15 — a per-*file* check over a file with 26 spawn sites

The test was a four-file loop whose whole body was `expect(src).toMatch(/wrapServerSpec\s*\(/)` — one token, anywhere in the file. `connector-spawns.ts` funnels 26 MCPClient spawns through a single `wrap` helper, so its token survives **any** per-site removal. The static `D10-wrap-spec` rule short-circuited per file too.

Reproduced against the real file: unwrapping one connector left **6 `wrapServerSpec(` tokens** in place, and both gates reported clean. The third gate — that connector's own spawner test — also passes, because only 6 of the file's spawner describes assert `.command`. The child would then run with a live OAuth token in its env and no landlock/seccomp/seatbelt profile, past three green checks.

Both checks are now **per site**: every `...connectorSpawn(` literal must be lexically enclosed by a `wrap(` / `wrapServerSpec(` call, resolved by walking back to the nearest open paren. Against the real tree that is 78 sites, zero violations, zero false positives.

The hardcoded four also omitted **`chatops-bot-spawn.ts`**, which has two real spawn sites. The list is now derived, behind a non-vacuity floor so a mis-globbed scan can't pass as a compliant tree.

## I4 — a forged `approved` row, and a grep that saw one file

`connectors/reindex.ts:122` wrote `hitlStatus: "approved"` on its `data.minimization.prune` audit row. `ipc/reindex-rpc.ts` gates `depth === "full"` alone, and the `full` branch returns `itemsAffected: 0` — so that row can **only** be emitted on a path where the gate was never entered. A consent decision that never happened, inside the verified hash chain: the S1-F5 / chain C6 shape the invariant exists to prevent. It now writes `not_required`, following the documented pattern at `federation-rpc.ts:543-546`.

The entire enforcement of I4 was one `read()` of `commands/data-delete.ts` and one `not.toMatch` — adding the string to any other file was invisible, and there is no static D-rule for I4. It now scans `packages/{gateway,cli,ui}/src` recursively against an **earned set** of five files, each carrying the gate that backs it. Every entry was checked against its gate rather than assumed: the set is deliberately *not* "the files that currently contain the string", which is how an allowlist becomes a laundering mechanism for the thing it polices. `reindex.ts` was in that population and is not in the set.

## I18 — an assertion satisfied by a type declaration

`expect(gate).toContain("isOperatorValid")` against `query-gate.ts`, where the only occurrence of that string is the ctx **type field**:

```ts
readonly identity?: { readonly enabled: boolean; readonly isOperatorValid: () => boolean };
```

The call lives in `_lib/gate-commons.ts` and the wiring in `ipc/federation-rpc.ts` — files the test never opened. Deleting the one line that supplies `ctx.identity` left it green, because `query-gate.ts` would be byte-identical.

The test's own title promised two things and asserted neither half about the first. There is now an assertion for each: the real call site, the wiring that feeds it, and a tree scan proving no module outside `identity/` verifies a JWT.

## I1 — a regex that did not match its own documented anti-pattern

`docs/SECURITY-INVARIANTS.md` writes the anti-pattern as `{ env: { ...process.env, EXTRA: ... } }`. The regex was `/\{\s*\.\.\.process\.env\s*\}/`, which requires `}` **immediately** after the spread — so it matched the bare form and missed the documented one. The comma form is what a real regression looks like, since the site being rewritten needs to add a variable alongside the inherited environment.

Its companion asserted `extensionProcessEnv(` appears **≥ 20** times against **80** real call sites, so 60 could regress and still pass — and `readDirConcat` swept in `*.test.ts`, so fixtures counted toward that floor, and was non-recursive, so a subdirectory was invisible. The floor is now derived: every `env:` under lazy-mesh is enumerated and classified, written as what *cannot* pass, with locals resolved back to their `extensionProcessEnv` binding rather than exempted.

## D22 — four assertions scanning for strings inside the functions being scanned for

`expect(audit).toContain("D22-connectors-dispatch")` and three siblings. All four literals are `rule:` fields **inside the check functions**. Deleting the `run()` block that invokes them leaves every assertion green while `audit:invariants` stops executing D22. Rules (b) and (c) survive that by luck — each has an independent tree-scan elsewhere. Rule (a), the `connectors.dispatch` confinement, has none. Now asserts the invocations, same shape as the scan-floor test in #1217.

## Red-prove

Every guard was reverted and confirmed to fail naming the right thing — mutations applied to real files, restored after, tree verified clean:

| Mutation | Failing test |
| --- | --- |
| `{ ...process.env, X }` into a lazy-mesh spawn | `contains no \`{ ...process.env\` spread` + `every env: … comes from extensionProcessEnv` |
| Unwrap one spawn site (6 wrapper tokens remain) | `every ServerSpec literal under lazy-mesh is enclosed` |
| `approved` row in a file outside the earned set | `no production file outside the earned set hardcodes hitlStatus` |
| Delete `identity: ctx.identityGuard` | `the federated gate CALLS isOperatorValid` |
| Delete the D22 invocation from `run()` | `D22 confines connectors.dispatch …` |

Docs updated in the same commit per the triple rule, including three claims that were simply false: I18's "size assertion 94" describes an assertion this file has never contained (`94` appears nowhere in it); I4's "the only production assignment site" was wrong by five; and I1's wiring counts said "30+ … `connector-spawns.ts` (16), `phase3-config.ts` (8)" against actual figures of 78, 31 and 45.

`bun run preflight:fast` — 29/29. `bun test packages/gateway/src/security-invariants.test.ts scripts/structure-audit` — 715 pass, 0 fail. Connector + lazy-mesh suites — 3,154 pass, 0 fail.

title: fix(coverage): gate four runtime-bearing types files and give the sandbox harness a way to run
body:
Findings from a coverage audit across all six repos, scored against the merged lcov from CI run `31945036362` using the repo's own `parseLcov` / `isExempt` / `checkScopes`. Only the cheap, verified items are acted on here; the rest are listed at the end for you to triage.

Headline for context, since it frames what is and isn't worth doing: Nimbus is at **97.46% lines / 92.73% branches** over 1,000 non-exempt files, all 24 scope gates pass with 7–27 points of slack, and the ratchet baseline carries **zero** debt entries. There is no coverage problem. There are exemption-hygiene problems, which is a different thing.

## 1. Four files were inheriting a name-pattern exemption they don't qualify for

`exclusions.ts` exempts `types.ts` / `-types.ts` by basename, and the comment on that regex is explicit about the deal:

> read them as "matched by name, not verified" — a new `types.ts` that grows runtime logic must be added to `NEVER_EXEMPT`, not left to inherit an exemption it does not deserve.

Auditing the 28 name-matched files found four that had grown exactly that, and none were listed:

| File | What it actually carries |
| --- | --- |
| `decisions/decision-source-types.ts` | `DECISION_SOURCE_TYPES` + `decisionSourceFilter()` — **builds SQL** (`{ sql, params }`) |
| `glossary/glossary-source-types.ts` | same shape, same SQL-building |
| `extensions/auto-update-types.ts` | `ACTION_TYPE_AUTO_UPDATE` / `ACTION_TYPE_DOWNGRADE` — the action-type strings `auto-update-rpc.ts` puts on the action it sends to the consent gate, i.e. what I2/I3 match on |
| `perf/types.ts` | `S8_LENGTHS` / `S8_BATCHES`, iterated to derive benchmark surface ids |

**All four measure 100 line / 100 branch on the CI lcov** (real records: LF=5, 5, 2, 2), so this buys no debt at all — it buys the regression guard they were silently outside of. Verified with `isExempt` before and after: the four now gate, and an arbitrary `some/other-types.ts` still inherits the exemption, so the general rule is intact.

## 2. A harness cited as a coverage layer, which had no way to run

`sonar-project.properties` justified excluding every connector's `src/server.ts` partly like this:

> only the sandbox harness (gated on `NIMBUS_TEST_HARNESS`) can run it

`NIMBUS_TEST_HARNESS` is read in **79** places — one `describe.skipIf` per connector — and was set in **none**. No workflow, no script, no documented command. A plain `bun test` reported all 79 as skipped, and always had.

**My first read of this was wrong and worth recording**, because the correction is the useful part. I assumed the fix was to enable them in CI, and started down that road. Running all 79 locally gives 78 pass / 1 fail, and chasing the failure is what showed why that would have been a bad change: `runSandboxContractTests` forks a probe that opens a **real network connection** to the connector's first declared `permissions.network` host. The one failure is `wiz`, and it is environmental — `api.app.wiz.io` does not resolve from here (`curl` exit 6) while `api.github.com` returns 200. The manifest is fine.

So gating these off by default is **correct**, not an oversight: they are live outbound traffic to ~79 vendor endpoints. What was missing was any way to run them at all, and a Sonar note that claimed they were doing work they were not.

Added `bun run test:sandbox`, which sets the variable and discovers the set (so it does not carry a list that goes stale as connectors are added), and accepts a path to scope to one connector. Env passthrough is explicit because `NIMBUS_TEST_HARNESS=1 bun test …` is a POSIX-shell idiom and a parse error in PowerShell (Non-Negotiable 5).

**Red-proved** — the same file, two ways:

```
plain bun test  ->  0 pass  1 skip  0 fail
bun run test:sandbox  ->  1 pass  0 fail
```

That difference is the entire claim, so it is the thing I checked. The Sonar note now says what is true, including that a non-resolving host is an environment result rather than a manifest defect.

## 3. A CI step label that misstates the gate it runs

`_test-suite.yml` named the step **"Coverage floor — per-file 80% gate"**. It has been `FLOOR_PCT = 85` line / `BRANCH_FLOOR_PCT = 80` branch since those constants landed. The label is what people read in the checks list when deciding whether a red gate applies to them.

## Verification

`preflight:fast` — 29 of 29, exit 0, run again after rebasing onto `main` at 2.4.8. `audit:exclusion-parity` green (it is the gate that would catch a Sonar/registry mismatch from §1 and §2). New discovery helper has four tests, including that it matches `sandbox.test.ts` but not `sandbox-helpers.test.ts`, and returns forward slashes on every platform.

## Not done — findings that need a decision, not a drive-by

- **The `Vault ≥90%` scope gate is close to vacuous.** It is computed over **4 files / 31 executable lines** — `darwin-keychain-status.ts` (11), `index.ts` (0), `key-format.ts` (8), `mock.ts` (12) — and one of the four is a test double. The vault directory is 887 lines. `vault/win32.ts`, which carries **I12**, has **no lcov record at all**, and `check-scopes.ts` already says so in a comment. Reaching 100% there proves very little. Worth reshaping, but that is a real piece of work and it changes what a headline number in `CLAUDE.md` means.
- **`expectNoRejectedDiagnostics`** is published from `@nimbus-dev/sdk/testing`, documented, exported and untested — but has **zero** consumers anywhere in `packages/`, so it is an unused published API rather than a live risk. (An earlier draft of this audit called it "the mechanism every connector uses to fail its own suite". It is not; that claim was checked against the consumers and dropped.)
- **Four satellite repos guard their Sonar step with `if: env.SONAR_TOKEN != ''`**, which makes the workflow green while analysing nothing. `create-nimbus-connector` deliberately refuses that guard and documents why, skipping only on fork PRs where GitHub withholds secrets. That is the pattern the other four should copy — the fix already exists in the fleet.
- **86 connector shell files / ~11,189 lines carry no lcov data**, which is the intended consequence of the `server.ts` + `tools.ts` exclusions, not a regression.
- **Nimbus is the only repo in the fleet with a per-file branch floor.** `create-nimbus-connector` gates lines+functions, the three vitest repos gate nothing per-file, and Sonar's gate is new-code only.

title: feat(clips): related answers about the resolved item, and its snippets come from the body
body:
Three changes to `POST /v1/clips/related`, driven by the browser clipper's Related panel. Two of them are defects that shipped, not gaps.

## The snippet has always been an extract of the title

`snippet()`'s second argument is an FTS5 **column index**, and V48 re-pointed `item_fts` from `(title, body_preview)` to `(title, body)` — so index `0` is the title. The browser panel renders that snippet directly beneath the same title, which is why the lane reads thin: its second line was its first line again.

Now index `1`, with a 24-token budget. `COALESCE(..., '')` is load-bearing: `snippet()` over a NULL body returns SQL `NULL`, and the client's guard requires a string — a null would drop the whole hit from the panel rather than blank a line.

A negative index was considered and rejected: it auto-selects the best-matching column, which for the title-driven query below re-selects the title. Verified empirically against SQLite on Bun 1.3.14.

## `type` and `modified_at` are projected

Both are indexed columns on the table the query already reads. Purely additive; named as `GET /v1/items/resolve` names them (`type` plain, `modified_at` snake_case, epoch ms) so one client-side boundary parser serves both routes.

## `itemId` makes relatedness about the item, not the page title

The client resolves the page to an indexed item and could only send `document.title` — which on a pull request is mostly chrome, and on Jenkins is `build #42 [Jenkins]`. `RelatedInput.itemId` now takes that item's **title** as the query and drops the item from its own results.

Its title, never its body: `ftsMatchQuery` AND-joins every token, so a 16 KiB body becomes thousands of required terms and matches nothing.

Two rules are deliberately **independent**: query-text precedence is `selection` → `itemId` → `title`, while self-exclusion fires whenever `itemId` is *present and resolves* — not when it wins. Otherwise selecting a phrase on PR #482 would return PR #482 as its own top hit. An unknown id falls through to the title path rather than erroring, since the row may have been deleted between resolve and related.

## Notes

- The host-exclusion rule is untouched. The client stops sending `canonicalUrl` once it can name the item, so the filter simply stops firing on work surfaces — no contract semantics changed.
- `glossary-project.ts` had a comment claiming `item_fts` indexes `body_preview`; V48 made that untrue. Comment-only fix.

Tests: 316 pass across clips + glossary. Typecheck and Biome clean.

Browser-client half: `nimbus-web-clipper` `feat/richer-related-lane`.

title: feat(agents): make built-in brief synthesis executable
body:
Built-in agent brief synthesis has existed since 2026-05-09 (`agents/_lib/synthesize.ts`) but had
never actually run in production: `AgentsRpcContext.runner` was `undefined` at both production
dispatchers (`ipc/server/dispatchers.ts`'s socket path and `agent-runs/agent-http-invoke.ts`'s HTTP
path), so every built-in brief took the deterministic, non-LLM render path regardless of `[llm]`
settings. This PR wires that seam through to production.

**User-visible behaviour change: with Ollama running, this is on by default.** `[agents] synthesis`
defaults to `"local"`, not `"off"` — so on any machine where a local `LlmProvider` (Ollama or
llama.cpp) answers, the prose of all fourteen built-in briefs (catchup, conflicts, expert, ghost,
huddle, impact, janitor, preflight, why, glossary, decisions, ownership, premortem, negotiate) is
now model-rewritten instead of deterministically rendered. And on a machine where Ollama answers
but the configured `[llm] local_model` is not pulled, every brief now gains a
"_Rendered deterministically — a synthesis was attempted and discarded (...)_" footer where it
previously had a clean deterministic render with no such note — the render itself is unchanged,
but a rewrite was attempted and failed first. Set `[agents] synthesis = "off"` to opt out entirely
and return to the pre-this-PR behaviour.

### What changed

- New `[agents] synthesis` config: `"off" | "local" | "allow-remote"` (default `"local"`).
  `"off"` never attempts a rewrite. `"local"` attempts synthesis whenever a runner is invoked, but
  a resolved provider that turns out to be non-local (not `ollama`/`llamacpp`) is refused as
  `no_eligible_provider` rather than used — so "a local provider answers" is necessary but not
  sufficient; the mode can still refuse even when Ollama is healthy, if the registered Ollama model
  falls below `[llm].min_reasoning_params` (the reasoning capability floor `selectProvider`
  enforces for every task, `resolveForSynthesis` included) and a remote provider is registered to
  fall through to. `"allow-remote"` additionally permits a non-local provider — see below for what
  "prefers" means under that mode.
- Per-invocation provider resolution (`agents/_lib/synthesis-llm.ts`) — never cached, since a local
  provider such as Ollama can start or stop under a long-lived Gateway process.
- A `requiredPhrases` honesty guard (`agents/_lib/brief-contract.ts`) that discards a synthesized
  rewrite if it drops a section's contractually-required disclaimer text, checked against a
  normalized, per-heading-scoped section body so a model that re-formats or reorders text isn't
  mistaken for one that deleted the disclaimer.
- A new `model`-class egress-ledger row (I29, raised from `none` coverage to `per-call`) appended by
  `egress/synthesis-egress.ts`'s `recordSynthesisEgress` before any REMOTE generate call. The
  local/remote split is enforced inside the appender via a required `remote` argument, not left to
  the caller: a local-provider generation appends nothing, not even a blocked row.
- Rejection provenance (`timeout` / `contract_violation` / `provider_error` /
  `egress_append_failed` / `empty_result`) carried on the `briefReady` notification's new
  `synthesis` field (`.synthesis.attempted` / `.synthesis.reason`), and on the HTTP
  `GET /v1/agents/runs/{id}` response, so "why is this brief still deterministic?" is answerable
  without a debug build.
- `nimbus prove`'s `COVERAGE_CLASS_LABELS` gains a `model` entry ("remotely-synthesized agent
  briefs") so the scope line never falls through to a bare, unlabeled key.
- `LlmRouter.resolveForSynthesis()` now accepts an explicit `preferLocal` argument (default
  `config.preferLocal`, so every other caller is unaffected) instead of always reading
  `config.preferLocal` implicitly. Agent brief synthesis passes the literal `true`: **under BOTH
  `"local"` and `"allow-remote"`, brief synthesis prefers a local provider regardless of
  `[llm] prefer_local`, falling back to remote only when no local provider answers (or a resolved
  local provider is skipped by the reasoning capability floor above).** This only reorders
  priority — `firstAvailable` still walks the whole provider list, so a registered remote provider
  stays reachable under `"allow-remote"` exactly as before; it changes tie-breaking, not
  permission, and only in the less-egress direction. Without this, `[llm] prefer_local = false`
  with a remote provider registered would make priority remote-first, so `"local"` mode could
  refuse a synthesis attempt even with a healthy local Ollama.
  Precedent, stated accurately: `briefs/brief-llm-adapter.ts`'s `createBriefLlm(router,
  briefsToml.preferLocal)` passes a **configurable** `[briefs] prefer_local` key
  (`nimbus-toml.ts`, default `true`) — that precedent establishes "a surface may override
  `[llm].prefer_local` with its own knob," not "a surface may hardcode it." This PR hardcodes the
  literal `true` rather than adding a matching `[agents] synthesis_prefer_local` key; an
  operator-configurable equivalent, if ever wanted, is a natural follow-up, not something today's
  config already provides.

### Honest limits — please read before merging

- **The `requiredPhrases` guard covers only `negotiate` today.** All seven of `negotiate`'s
  null-lane disclaimers ("could not be computed") are enforced. Every other brief kind — including
  `decisions`'s and `premortem`'s 0.86 confidence ceiling, and the `body_complete = 0` truncation
  counts `glossary`/`decisions`/`premortem` each render — returns an empty `requiredPhrases` set
  (`brief-contract.ts`'s explicit switch, not a fallthrough, so a fifteenth brief kind is a compile
  error rather than a silent gap). A synthesized rewrite of those kinds could silently drop either
  disclosure today; widening the guard is a follow-up, not a hidden omission.
- **`"allow-remote"` is presently unreachable in production.** `packages/gateway/src/llm/` ships
  exactly two `LlmProvider` implementations, `OllamaProvider` and `LlamaCppProvider` — both local —
  and `platform/assemble.ts` registers only those two. No remote provider exists anywhere in the
  tree, so `recordSynthesisEgress` cannot be called with `remote: true` today. The `model` egress
  class is wired end-to-end and raised to `per-call` coverage, but appends zero rows in production
  until a remote provider ships.
- **The default mode is `"local"`, so a stock install cannot egress a brief.** `"allow-remote"` is
  opt-in for exactly that reason — it is the first path by which indexed content could leave the
  machine without a connector involved, once a remote provider exists to reach it.
- **A timed-out generation is abandoned, not cancelled.** `LlmGenerateOptions` carries no
  `AbortSignal`, so `synthesisTimeoutMs` (default 20000ms) bounds how long the caller waits, not how
  long the underlying provider call keeps running.
